case: Bill Ackman and Pershing Square buying credit-index CDS protection during the COVID shock

source_summary.setup: Pershing Square believed COVID would force Europe and the U.S. into shutdowns, hitting equities and corporate credit simultaneously.
source_summary.portfolio_choice: Pershing chose to hedge rather than sell its long book because it still believed its portfolio companies would recover and create long-term value.
source_summary.instrument: Pershing bought CDS protection on broad credit indices: CDX IG, CDX HY, and iTraxx Europe.
source_summary.core_thesis: Corporate credit spreads were far too tight for the impending economic stop. Investment-grade credit indices were around 50 bps per year, near all-time tights, and high-yield spreads were also near lows.
source_summary.mechanism: This was primarily a spread-widening trade, not a default trade. Pershing needed credit spreads to gap wider as markets priced shutdown, liquidity stress, recession risk, and refinancing risk.
source_summary.convexity: Large notional protection at low starting spreads created large mark-to-market upside if spreads widened sharply.
source_summary.execution_window: Use 2020-02-28 as the eval trade date, representing the end of the last week of February when the hedge would have been put on or substantially built.
source_summary.documentation_context: On March 3, 2020, Pershing said it had taken steps during the prior ten days to protect the portfolio from downward market volatility. That supports the late-February execution window but is not the trade date.
source_summary.exit_context: By March 9 and March 12, the hedge had appreciated substantially. Pershing began selling as spreads widened and the risk/reward became less attractive.
source_summary.trade_after_trade: Pershing recycled hedge proceeds into equities and risk assets during the crash, adding to or repurchasing high-quality long positions.

selected_details: Pershing used CDX IG, CDX HY, and iTraxx Europe CDS indices.
Investment-grade spreads were described as around 50 bps per year, near all-time tight levels.
The trade did not require mass defaults; it required credit spreads to widen sharply.
A move from 50 bps to 150 bps on five-year IG CDS can create a large mark-to-market gain equal to roughly the present value of the spread difference.
The eval uses a late-February execution window, represented by 2020-02-28.
By March 9, 2020, the CDS position was worth about $1.8 billion.
By March 12, 2020, the CDS position was worth about $2.75 billion.
Pershing completed the hedge exit by March 23, 2020, with about $2.6 billion of proceeds against about $27 million of premiums and commissions.
Pershing recycled proceeds into equities including Agilent, Berkshire Hathaway, Hilton, Lowe's, Howard Hughes, Restaurant Brands, and Starbucks.

future_outcome_context.notes: The March 3 disclosure, March 9 and March 12 hedge values, and March 23 exit results are documentation/outcome context, not initiation-date evidence for 2020-02-28.

human_notes: Historical source case supplied by the user. The lesson is not 'pandemic means buy CDS'; it is that a direct, convex hedge can be actionable when a near-term systemic shock is underpriced and the instrument references the variable likely to reprice.
